summary.text: A Robert Trent Jones Sr. course from 1980 on the Troia peninsula, between the Atlantic and the Sado estuary, reached by a short ferry from Setubal.

setting.text: Sits on the Troia peninsula, wedged between the Atlantic, the Sado Estuary and the Serra da Arrabida.
You reach it by a short ferry crossing from Setubal, which a Golfshake writer put at 15 minutes.
Golfshake describes a long, flat sandy strip at sea level, with the Arrabida mountains as a backdrop.
Portugalgolf.net says the main obstacle is sand, which lines the whole course.
Golfshake says fairways are narrow and hemmed in by sandy dunes and pine trees, with small greens, defensive bunkers, swales and hummocks.
Jones's usual style is here: bold bunkering, raised greens and doglegs sweeping between pine trees.
A Golfshake reviewer loved it but said it needs full concentration, calling it a roller coaster of easier holes followed by much harder ones.

history.text: Opened in 1980, designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr.
The 1983 Portuguese Open was played here. Sam Torrance won on 286, two under par, three strokes clear of Chris Moody.
Top100golfcourses says Torrance was the only player to beat par for the championship.
Golfshake says Golf World ranked it 32nd on Continental Europe, and that it was named among the world's best courses by Rolex in 2011.
The resort says Golf World magazine voted Troia one of Continental Europe's best 10 resorts in 2019.
Golfshake says the course was bought and is managed by Arrow's management company, Details, with new ownership in 2025.
Top100golfcourses says it had Troia ranked fourth in Portugal when its 2026 ranking was released, then noted it would be closed in 2026 under new ownership.
The resort says the course is closed for a renovation expected to last 12 months, with reopening scheduled for early 2027 and a new clubhouse planned.

trivia.text: Golfshake describes a par 72 of 6,317 metres.
Top100golfcourses calls Troia magnificent, engaging and highly underrated.
Top100golfcourses advises picking the right tee box, saying Troia is 'no place to be macho'.
Top100golfcourses' Portugal ranking history says Troia rose two places to fourth in 2016.

1.text: Portugalgolf.net says the opening par five asks for a drive over a sizeable lake from the back tee, to a green so closely bunkered that reaching it in two is hard.

2.text: Portugalgolf.net calls the 2nd a stunning par three with the green on the edge of the beach.

3.text: A 368-metre par four that Top100golfcourses calls one of the finest sea holes in Portugal.
Portugalgolf.net says Robert Trent Jones Sr. considered the 3rd, a par four with a sea view, one of the best he ever designed.
A Golfshake reviewer said Jones followed the natural contours and used the sandy waste areas to define the play, calling it a gem.

4.text: A short par three of about 123 metres where wind off the ocean is a real factor, according to a Golfshake reviewer.

7.text: A Golfshake reviewer called the par-five 7th the hardest hole, needing an accurate tee shot and a precise approach to a heavily guarded green.

11.text: A Golfshake reviewer said the tee on this par three is set slightly off-line from the green, which can throw your alignment.

14.text: A Golfshake reviewer described the par-five 14th as a double dogleg that turns the round towards home and the Atlantic.

17.text: A Golfshake reviewer said the par-three 17th runs parallel to the ocean and beach with sandy waste that makes it feel like an island green, and found it the easiest hole.

18.text: Portugalgolf.net says the 18th is a par five dogleg left with an elevated green protected by three front bunkers.

local.text: Setubal is about a 30-minute drive from Lisbon, with the ferry crossing to Troia a further 15 minutes.
Golfshake says Comporta is about 30 minutes away by car.
A Golfshake reviewer noted a purpose-built marina at Troia for those combining yachting with golf.

Golfshake describes the Roman ruins at Troia as the largest known fish-salting facility in the Roman world, and a reviewer says the ferry crossing included learning about a resident pod of bottlenose dolphins.
